text:
sam: :rotating_light: SLO burn in us-west for hosted-infer gateway p99 timeouts, started ~05:07 UTC. Alert shows a 3x increase in 5xx/timeouts. Dashboard: https://console.redwood-infer/internal/dashboards/ingress-slo?from=3798762000
alert-manager: SLO burn alert - hosted-infer.gateway.p99 > 800ms (5m) - triggered
devops-bot: sampling-rate for traces in us-west is 10% (configured). Missing spans flagged for many requests.
alex: throwing up some queries — checking logs/edges. Can you paste the alert query? Also any customer impact tickets?
sam: alert query: `sum(rate(gateway_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"ingress\",le=\"0.99\"}[5m])) by (region)` and `count_over_time(gateway_response{status=~\"5..\"}[5m])` — p99 jumps coincide with 5xx spikes
maria: support received 3 related tickets: #C-23344 #C-23345 #C-23346. Customers report reply delays and occasional 502s. Support attaching example request IDs.
support-agent: attaching request ids: `req=9f1a2b`, `req=7c3d4e`, `req=2b9c8a`. All last-hop failures show `upstream: connection reset by peer`
oncall-rotator: repro steps I'm running: `curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -d '{"input":"echo"}' https://api.usw2.rw-infer/v1/generate` — saw `502` within 2s consistently from one AZ
alex: checking x-forwarded-for & LB health, also looking at prefetch/batcher logs. Query I'm running: `logs | filter component=\"upstream-proxy\" and status_code >= 500 | stats count() by upstream_host` — early results show one backend with burst errors
devops-bot: note: prefetch pool CPU on node `gpu-14b-usw2` spiked at the same time. Kernel 5.10 driver logs show ephemeral handshake timeouts
maria: any tracing gaps? Customers complaining they get no spans for the failing requests
alex: yes — many traces missing KV-cache spans. Looks like tracer sampling + a bug in proxy tracing header propagation when request is hit by a cold-worker fallback
sam: hypothesis: sudden burst -> prefetch backpressure -> cold-worker fallback -> tracing header dropped -> no spans and 502s
maria: potential quick mitigations: (1) increase trace sampling for alerts to 100% for 10m in us-west, (2) temporarily route traffic off `gpu-14b-usw2` pool, (3) enable fallback throttling
oncall-rotator: I disabled `gpu-14b-usw2` from LB rotation at 05:15 UTC, rerouted to healthy nodes. Retrying customer requests now.
support-agent: updated tickets with mitigation steps and ETA. Customers notified.
alex: after removing node, 5xx rate dropped to baseline in 3m. Need postmortem: root cause likely node-level NIC flapping under prefetch CPU pressure. Will open a follow-up infra issue.
devops-bot: created infra incident: INC-2026-0479, linked to this thread
maria: runbook updates: add quick-checks for prefetch CPU + kernel handshake errors, and a playbook to drain nodes faster. I'll draft.
sam: good. Assigning action items: alex -> infra issue, maria -> runbook draft, oncall-rotator -> full repro log bundle, support-agent -> close customer loop. :thumbsup:
alert-manager: alert resolved - hosted-infer.gateway.p99 back to normal
alex: putting a follow-up in monday's eng-sre sync to discuss long-term fix (batcher backpressure + tracing header hardening)
maria: adding tracelog query to diagnostics doc: `trace | where trace_id in (...) and has(span.name, \"kv-cache\")` — will paste in doc
oncall-rotator: uploading logs: https://s3.redwood-infer/incidents/INC-2026-0479/log-bundle.tar.gz
sam: thanks everyone, closing this thread after PMR is posted
maria: :white_check_mark:
